standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that det_kappa(L) is generated by any single symbol attached to an admissible sequence generating L, which is what makes gamma surjective; the construction of gamma and the verification of its three properties stay inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Make the rule [e_1, ..., e_k] tensor [fbar_1, ..., fbar_m] -> [e_1, ..., e_k, f_1, ..., f_m] well defined despite the concatenation of admissible sequences not being admissible in general: a nonzero symbol [e_1, ..., e_k] forces K = <e_1, ..., e_k>, in which case the concatenation is admissible and the value is independent of the lifts f_i by relation (b) of det_kappa(L), and then each admissible relation in K or in M transfers to the concatenated sequence (proof lines 16298-16319).

Deduce that gamma is an isomorphism rather than only a linear map: det_kappa(L) is generated by a single symbol of any admissible sequence generating L, so the map is surjective onto a one dimensional space (proof lines 16322-16328).

Verify property (1) by evaluating det_kappa(v) on the concatenated symbol and identifying the result with gamma composed with det_kappa(u) tensor det_kappa(w) (proof lines 16331-16339), and verify property (2) by showing that the two expressions differ by (-1)^{cg} using relation (c) cg times in the order that moves each zeta_j past gamma_c, ..., gamma_1 (proof lines 16340-16362); property (3) is immediate.
proof_roadmap: Establish well definedness of gamma on symbols, using that a nonzero symbol generates the whole module and that relation (b) absorbs the choice of lifts (proof lines 16298-16319).
Get surjectivity from the single-symbol generation of det_kappa(L) (proof lines 16322-16328).

Check the three stated properties: the functioniality square by direct evaluation, the sign square by an ordered application of the admissible relation of type (c), and the kappa-vector-space case as immediate (proof lines 16331-16365).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs a canonical map gamma from det_kappa(K) tensor det_kappa(M) to det_kappa(L) on nonzero symbols [e_1, ..., e_k] tensor [fbar_1, ..., fbar_m] -> [e_1, ..., e_k, f_1, ..., f_m] and asserts three properties: equivariance for isomorphisms of short exact sequences, a square with a Koszul sign (-1)^{cg}, and agreement with the usual determinant isomorphism for kappa-vector spaces (statement lines 16202-16295, with two commutative diagrams drawn in Xy-pic). The subtlety is well definedness on nonzero symbols: an admissible sequence in K and one in M need not concatenate to an admissible sequence in L, and the value must be independent of the chosen lifts; the author resolves this by observing that a nonzero symbol forces K = <e_1, ..., e_k>, and then transfers each admissible relation separately (proof lines 16298-16319). Surjectivity of gamma is obtained from the generation statement for det_kappa(L) of the previous lemmas rather than from a direct computation (proof lines 16322-16328), and property (2) is a genuine sign computation carried out by applying the admissible relation of type (c) a total of cg times in a prescribed order (proof lines 16340-16362). The claim is a nontrivial diagram-level consistency statement, so it is H2.
